## TL;DR

Organic aerosols ($\text{OA}$) make up $20–90\%$ of fine particulate mass, but where the mass sits and where it kills are almost mirror images. A source-resolved volatility-basis-set model in $\text{CESM2}$ attributes over $85\%$ of the $1.28$ million annual $\text{OA}$ deaths to fossil-fuel and residential combustion, which carry a minority of the mass, while biogenic forest terpenes supply $-0.32\text{ W m}^{-2}$ of remote cooling. After this module you can explain why cutting fossil emissions saves lives at little cost in aerosol climate masking.
:::

## Three sources of organic aerosol

**Organic aerosols (OA)** are carbonaceous particles suspended in the atmosphere. They come from three source classes:

1. **Fossil Fuel Combustion ($\text{ffOA}$)**: Emitted directly as primary particles and formed as secondary aerosols from vehicle tailpipes, industrial boilers, and power plants. Concentrated heavily in densely populated urban corridors.
2. **Biomass & Biofuel Burning ($\text{bbOA}$)**: Emitted from wildfires, agricultural crop residue burning, and residential wood/coal cookstoves. Characterized by **brown carbon ($\text{BrC}$)** that absorbs ultraviolet and visible sunlight[^1].
3. **Biogenic Secondary Organic Aerosols ($\text{bSOA}$)**: Formed when volatile organic compounds ($\text{VOCs}$) emitted by trees and vegetation (isoprene, $\alpha$-pinene, sesquiterpenes) oxidize in sunlight into low-volatility condensable vapors[^2].

## Mass and mortality are decoupled

The central result of our study in *Environmental Science & Technology*[^3] is that **the global mass budget of organic aerosols is decoupled from its health burden**:

- **Mass vs. Location**: Biogenic $\text{bSOA}$ accounts for nearly $60–70\%$ of total global organic aerosol mass burden. However, because forests are located far from dense megacities, humans inhale only a tiny fraction of biogenic particles.
- **Toxicity and Proximity**: Fossil fuel $\text{ffOA}$ represents only $\sim 15\%$ of global mass, but because it is emitted at ground level in urban centers alongside toxic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons ($\text{PAHs}$) and heavy metals, it accounts for the vast majority of human cardiopulmonary mortality.

## Source-resolved results from CESM2

To separate the pathways, we implemented a source-resolved **Volatility Basis Set (VBS)** parameterization inside the Community Earth System Model ($\text{CESM2} / \text{CAM6-chem}$), tracking chemical aging, gas-particle partitioning and optical properties of each source sector independently:

| Sector | Global Burden ($\text{Tg}$) | Direct Radiative Forcing ($\text{W m}^{-2}$) | Cloud Indirect Forcing ($\text{W m}^{-2}$) | Annual Premature Deaths |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Fossil Fuel ($\text{ffOA}$)** | $0.28\text{ Tg}$ | $-0.04\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | $-0.09\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | **$810,000$ deaths** |
| **Biomass / Biofuel ($\text{bbOA}$)** | $0.52\text{ Tg}$ | $+0.02\text{ W m}^{-2}$ (BrC warming) | $-0.14\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | **$390,000$ deaths** |
| **Biogenic SOA ($\text{bSOA}$)** | $1.41\text{ Tg}$ | $-0.12\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | $-0.20\text{ W m}^{-2}$ | **$80,000$ deaths** |
| **Total Combined** | **$2.21\text{ Tg}$** | **$-0.14\text{ W m}^{-2}$** | **$-0.43\text{ W m}^{-2}$** | **$1,280,000$ deaths** |

### Explore the sector trade-offs

Cut each sector separately and compare lives saved against the cooling given up:

```{=html}
<div style="background: var(--md-code-bg-color, #1e293b); border: 1px solid var(--md-typeset-table-color, #334155); border-radius: 12px; padding: 20px; margin: 24px 0; color: #e2e8f0; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;">

  <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)); gap: 14px; margin-bottom: 16px;">

      <label style="font-size: 0.85em; color: #ef4444;">Fossil Fuel (ffOA) Cut: <b id="ff-val">50%</b></label>

      <label style="font-size: 0.85em; color: #f59e0b;">Residential/Biomass (bbOA) Cut: <b id="bb-val">30%</b></label>

    </div>

      <label style="font-size: 0.85em; color: #10b981;">Biogenic Terpene Feedback Shift: <b id="bio-val">0%</b></label>
      <input type="range" id="sim-bio" min="-50" max="50" value="0" step="5" oninput="updateOaSim()" style="width: 100%;">

      <div style="font-size: 0.75em; color: #94a3b8; text-transform: uppercase;">Annual Lives Saved</div>
      <div id="oa-deaths" style="font-size: 1.4em; font-weight: 700; color: #10b981; margin-top: 4px;">522,000</div>
    </div>
    <div style="background: #0f172a; padding: 14px; border-radius: 8px; text-align: center; border-top: 3px solid #38bdf8;">

      <div id="oa-forcing" style="font-size: 1.4em; font-weight: 700; color: #f59e0b; margin-top: 4px;">+0.10 W/m²</div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div id="oa-text" style="font-size: 0.9em; background: rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.1); border-left: 4px solid #38bdf8; padding: 10px; border-radius: 4px;">
    Slashing fossil fuel emissions yields massive, immediate public health benefits in urban centers while producing a minimal loss of aerosol masking cooling.
  </div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<script>
function updateOaSim() {
  const ffCut = parseFloat(document.getElementById('sim-ff').value) / 100;
  const bbCut = parseFloat(document.getElementById('sim-bb').value) / 100;
  const bioShift = parseFloat(document.getElementById('sim-bio').value) / 100;

  document.getElementById('ff-val').innerText = Math.round(ffCut * 100) + '%';
  document.getElementById('bb-val').innerText = Math.round(bbCut * 100) + '%';
  document.getElementById('bio-val').innerText = (bioShift > 0 ? '+' : '') + Math.round(bioShift * 100) + '%';

  // Base mortalities
  const ffDeaths = 810000;
  const bbDeaths = 390000;
  const bioDeaths = 80000;

  const savedDeaths = Math.round(ffDeaths * ffCut + bbDeaths * bbCut - bioDeaths * bioShift);
  
  // Forcing calculation (loss of negative forcing = positive delta)
  const ffForcingDelta = 0.13 * ffCut;
  const bbForcingDelta = 0.12 * bbCut;
  const bioForcingDelta = -0.32 * bioShift;

  const netForcing = (ffForcingDelta + bbForcingDelta + bioForcingDelta).toFixed(2);

  document.getElementById('oa-deaths').innerText = savedDeaths.toLocaleString() + ' lives';
  document.getElementById('oa-forcing').innerText = (netForcing > 0 ? '+' : '') + netForcing + ' W/m²';

  let txt = '';
  if (ffCut > 0.6) {
    txt = '🌟 Aggressive fossil fuel phase-out eliminates over half a million deaths per year in Asia and Europe, proving clean energy is the ultimate health intervention.';
  } else if (bbCut > 0.5) {
    txt = '🔥 Clean cookstove transitions in Africa and South Asia drastically reduce indoor smoke mortality and brown carbon warming.';
  } else {
    txt = 'Balanced source-specific emission management optimizes the trade-off between clean air standards and global radiative equilibrium.';
  }
  document.getElementById('oa-text').innerText = txt;
}
window.addEventListener('load', updateOaSim);
setTimeout(updateOaSim, 300);
</script>
```


### Data and code

- **Global Climate Model**: The source-resolved organic aerosol VBS module is integrated within **CESM2.2 / CAM6-chem**[^4].
- **Health Exposure Calculations**: Population-weighted $\text{PM}_{2.5}$ exposure calculations follow the **Global Burden of Disease (GBD 2019)** methodology.
- **Source Scripts**: Data processing and plotting routines are available on GitHub: [`kamingfung/CESM-Organic-Aerosols`](https://github.com/kamingfung).

## Key takeaways

- Biogenic SOA is $60–70\%$ of global $\text{OA}$ mass but only about $6\%$ of $\text{OA}$ deaths, because forest terpene chemistry happens far from where people breathe.
- Fossil-fuel $\text{OA}$ is roughly $15\%$ of the mass and $65\%$ of the deaths ($810{,}000$ a year), because it is emitted at ground level in cities alongside PAHs and heavy metals.
- The "aerosol masking dilemma" does not apply to fossil $\text{OA}$: it supplies little cooling ($-0.13\text{ W m}^{-2}$ direct plus indirect), so phasing it out is a health win with minimal climate penalty.
- Biomass and biofuel $\text{OA}$ carries brown carbon that warms ($+0.02\text{ W m}^{-2}$ direct); replacing residential cookstoves removes toxic indoor smoke and a warming term at once.
- Mass burden is the wrong metric for health policy; exposure and toxicity are what scale.

[^3]: Jo, D. S., Nault, B. A., Tilmes, S., Gettelman, A., McCluskey, C. S., Hodzic, A., Fung, K. M. et al. Global health and climate effects of organic aerosols from different sources. *Environ. Sci. Technol.* **57**, 13793–13807 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.3c03544
